reasoning: The failure is a single-sided rollover caused by the robot's left wheels colliding with and climbing up a narrow vertical obstacle (furniture leg at lateral offset y ≈ +0.15 m, near the 0.17 m half-track of the robot) under high surface friction (indoor rug, μ ≈ 0.9) and low-to-moderate forward lunge speed (~0.25 m/s). To train a policy that avoids or safely handles grazing/climbing narrow obstacles on either side of its wheel track, we should randomize the obstacle's lateral position (`obs_y`) around the left wheel track and across to the right wheel track (or vary `lateral_offset` so the policy encounters both left- and right-side wheel strikes), the obstacle forward distance (`obs_x`), the obstacle radius (`obs_r`) to represent various furniture legs/posts, the approach speed (`observed_speed`) to account for uncertainty in the commanded lunge speed/torque, the tire-surface friction (`friction`) since high traction directly enabled wheel climbing rather than slipping, and small variations in `approach_angle_deg`.

ranges.why: Base is +0.15 m (left wheel track is around +0.17 m). Sampling down to -0.20 m and up to +0.25 m covers grazing strikes on the left wheel, inner chassis, and right wheel track (-0.17 m) so the policy learns symmetric obstacle clearance.
Base is 0.6 m (hard bound minimum is 0.5 m). Sampling 0.5 m to 1.5 m varies the reaction time and stopping/steering distance available before impacting the post/leg.
Base is 0.03 m (clamped to hard bound 0.05 m). Sampling up to 0.15 m covers thin chair/table legs up to thicker bollards and posts that still catch a single wheel.
Base is 0.25 m/s. The exact wheel speed/torque command during the final lunge is an unknown, and higher approach speeds (up to 0.8 m/s) make wheel-climb rollovers even faster and more severe.

Base is 0.9 (indoor rug). High traction caused the wheel to climb the obstacle rather than slip; varying from 0.6 to 1.3 tests both moderate-grip floors and high-grip carpets/rough concrete where wheel climb is most dangerous.
Base is 0.0 deg. Small heading variations (-15 to +15 deg) change the contact geometry between the leading tire and the cylindrical obstacle and simulate slight swerves prior to contact.
Base is 0.0 m. Adding ±0.10 m perturbation in the robot's initial lateral offset further diversifies the exact wheel-to-obstacle overlap.
